test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: During the period of 1947-1990, India's trade policy was largely characterized by:

options.text: An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.
A policy of free trade with minimal government intervention in international transactions.
A liberal import policy aimed at providing consumers with a wide range of goods.
An aggressive export-oriented strategy focused on global competitiveness.

solution:
The correct answer is __**An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's trade policy between 1947-1990 was focused on **self-reliance**, aiming to reduce dependence on foreign goods and foster domestic industries.
 
• The strategy of **import substitution industrialization (ISI)** was adopted to protect and promote local industries by imposing high tariffs and quantitative restrictions on imports.
 
• This policy was driven by the belief that economic independence was essential for political independence and to avoid exploitation by foreign powers.
 
• India emphasized the development of heavy industries and basic infrastructure through public sector enterprises, which were seen as a means to achieve self-sufficiency.
 
• The trade policy was restrictive, with controls on foreign exchange and limited engagement in global trade, aiming to insulate the domestic economy from external influences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI):**

 
 
• This strategy focuses on replacing imported goods with domestically produced goods to strengthen local industries.
 
• It was widely adopted by newly independent countries, including India, during the mid-20th century.
 
• While it initially boosted industrial growth, ISI often led to inefficiencies and a lack of competitiveness in global markets.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of India's Pre-1991 Trade Policy:**
 
 
• High tariffs and import licensing to discourage imports.
 
• Focus on heavy industries, public sector dominance, and central planning under the Five-Year Plans.
 
• Limited foreign direct investment (FDI) and restricted access to foreign technology.
 
 
 
• **Protectionism:**
 
 
• Protective measures such as tariffs, quotas, and subsidies were used to shield domestic industries from international competition.
 
• This approach aimed to nurture infant industries but often resulted in inefficiencies and lack of innovation.
 
 
 
• **Shift Post-1991:**
 
 
• India shifted to a liberalized trade regime in 1991, focusing on globalization, privatization, and economic reforms.
 
• The introduction of reforms marked a departure from protectionism to outward-oriented policies, integrating India into the global economy.
